question: On claude-code with Claude Sonnet 5.5, what does compacting at 300k or 400k instead of the CLI's own auto window change in the responses to each level, the level reached, the compactions and the re-reads after them, and the cost per level of six hours of play?
note: The operator wants a default compaction window chosen from this comparison, leans to about 400k, and the arms are auto, 300k and 400k per model (operator, 2026-11-10); the models are Claude Sonnet 5.5 on claude-code and GPT-6 Luna on codex, one run per square on a six-hour clock, and an arm that a CLI would silently equal to auto, or refuse as a cap, is dropped for that model rather than run (operator, 2026-10-20). This is the claude-code half, and the only one. The codex half is dropped whole: the pinned Codex 0.163.0 catalogue gives gpt-6-luna a 272,000-token window, so codex compacts at 244,800 on auto, and 300k and 400k are both at or above that cap, refused at the first turn (codexWindowCapRefusal); an auto arm alone compares nothing. All three arms run the release build harness-0.5-1803-ga4d4633f, pinned by digest, so only the window separates them. Its Claude Code 2.1.321 takes CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW ahead of any setting or server value and applies the smaller of it and the model's context, which the CLI's catalogue gives claude-sonnet-5-5 as 1,000,000 tokens, so both treatments are honoured and neither is capped (claudeWindowCapRefusal). The driver hands the CLI integer tokens and the CLI compacts about 33k below the window (its 20k summary reserve and 13k buffer): near 267k at 300k (probed on 2.1.309 with --debug) and near 367k at 400k (the same arithmetic, not probed). The control passes no window. In 2.1.321 no per-model default or experiment names claude-sonnet-5-5, so auto is the whole 1M window and compacts near 967k, unless the server sends a window for the account, which the image does not pin; the compaction records name the threshold each run met. The clock is e360's six hours (operator, 2026-10-20), and a window changes nothing until the context grows past it: version 3's 300k run compacted once in its six hours, so a 400k run may never reach 367k, and then 400k against auto reads as 'did not bind at this length', which is itself an answer for a default. The squares are laid side by side, never pooled into a score: model responses (the claude-code driver's turn is a hand-off to a fresh CLI context, not a model turn) and wall time to each level, and the level at the clock; the compactions, and the reads of the API reference, of search and of the scratchpad in the responses after each one against before it; and cost per level from per-response usage at list price. One run per square finds large differences, not small ones. The leash is e360's (idle 20 minutes, the no-XP watchdog off, the 12000-call guard), and the stop is the to-level-10 campaigns' level 10, which six hours seldom reaches: most runs play the whole clock, and one that gets there gives a time to level 10. resume is false: a resumed claude-code run starts a fresh CLI with none of its history, a compaction to nothing that no window chose, so a paused run is a spent attempt and the next starts fresh. One cell, the subscription lanes' calibration start. Assignments are the store row's: sub-sonnet-55 (Claude Sonnet 5.5 on claude-code), one run per square, on the first subscription lane (operator, 2026-10-23). Version 4 supersedes version 3, which ran on harness-0.5-1643-ge85bd729 (Claude Code 2.1.309): its 100k, 200k and 300k squares each played the six-hour clock, and its auto square spent its three attempts on operator stops. Version 4 changes the arms to the operator's of 2026-11-10 and the image to the release build deployed when it was written; the cell, the leash, the stop, resume and the attempt cap are version 3's. Version 3's runs are context for this one, on an older CLI, and not squares of it.

cells.note: The subscription lanes' scored start: the calibration cell.

arms.note: The control: no window passed, the CLI's own auto (the whole 1M window on claude-sonnet-5-5 unless the server sends one).
